# Cowrie

> Cowrie is a free and open-source SSH and Telnet honeypot. It pretends to be a vulnerable server, logs brute-force logins, records every command attackers type, saves the malware they upload, and sends it all to analysis tools as JSON.

Cowrie began in 2014 as a fork of the Kippo honeypot and is maintained on GitHub by a community of volunteer contributors. It is written in Python and released under the BSD license. cowrie.org is the community website of the open-source project; the source code and issue tracker live on GitHub and the reference documentation on docs.cowrie.org.

## Project

- [Homepage](https://cowrie.org/): what Cowrie does, with a recorded attacker session
- [Features](https://cowrie.org/features): how Cowrie works and what it records, with example output
- [Integrations](https://cowrie.org/integrations): output plugins for Elasticsearch, Splunk, Sentinel, MISP, hpfeeds, VirusTotal, Slack and more
- [About](https://cowrie.org/about): project history and maintainers
- [Contact](https://cowrie.org/contact): how to reach the project
- [Privacy policy](https://cowrie.org/privacy)

## Documentation and source

- [Documentation](https://docs.cowrie.org/en/stable): reference documentation for installing, configuring and running Cowrie
- [Installation guide](https://docs.cowrie.org/en/stable/INSTALL.html): step-by-step setup
- [Output plugins](https://docs.cowrie.org/en/stable/OUTPUT.html): configuration for each output destination
- [Source code](https://github.com/cowrie/cowrie): GitHub repository, issue tracker and pull requests
- [Releases](https://github.com/cowrie/cowrie/releases): changelog and version history
